synthesis:draft.headline: Last pre-interval POE50 forecast for SA1 for 2026-07-29 07:30–08:00 UTC (2026-07-29 17:30 ACST) was 2017.0 MW; actual was 1872.0 MW, an error of 145.0 MW (7.75%).
summary: Actual operational demand for that half-hour = 1872.0 MW [ev0627].
Forecast error (POE50 − actual) = 145.0 MW [ev0628] = 7.75% of actual [ev0629].
The 24-half-hour mean absolute error (MAE) for the reviewed window is 139.71 MW [ev0704].

numeric_claims.text: Error as percent of actual for 2026-07-29 07:30–08:00 UTC
Mean absolute error (MAE) for the 24 half-hours reviewed

possible_explanations.statement: The forecast model's POE50 might have overestimated demand for that half-hour relative to the realised conditions.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare POE50 values from forecast runs issued before and after 2026-07-29T04:27:00Z (the run that produced ev0626) to see whether POE50 was consistently higher than the realised value and whether subsequent runs moved toward ev0627; check those runs' POE50 evidence_ids returned by the forecast tool.

possible_explanations.statement: Actual demand might have been lower than forecast because conditions that affect demand changed nearer real time (for example, weather or unobserved demand-side actions) and so the pre-interval forecast did not reflect them.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare contemporaneous observational data (e.g. weather or other near-real-time indicators) at times around 2026-07-29T04:27:00Z and the interval ending 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z, and check whether later forecast runs reduced POE50; use the runs' issue times and evidence_ids listed in the compare tool output to track revisions.

possible_explanations.statement: The forecast error might be within the typical range for this window, given the reviewed-window MAE.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the 145.0 MW error [ev0628] to the window MAE 139.71 MW [ev0704] and to the distribution of absolute errors across the 24 half-hours in the compare tool's pairs to see if this half-hour is near typical magnitude.
